articles.title: October Heatwave-Like Conditions Leave People Sweltering Through Day and Night - businessnewsthisweek.com
articles.full_text:
Bhubaneswar, Oct. 4: October is traditionally associated with a gradual retreat of the monsoon and a shift towards more comfortable weather, but this year, several parts of Odisha are experiencing conditions that feel more like the peak of summer.
Representational Image
Scorching temperatures during the day, combined with oppressive humidity after sunset, have left residents struggling to find relief. The intense heat has made outdoor activities particularly uncomfortable, while the lack of respite at night has added to the discomfort.
The unusual weather pattern has raised concerns among residents, especially those who have to commute or work outdoors for long hours. Even after the sun goes down, high humidity is making the atmosphere feel stifling, with many people reporting difficulty sleeping and remaining comfortable indoors.
Weather conditions during this period are being closely watched as October progresses, particularly amid concerns over possible changes in atmospheric conditions over the Bay of Bengal.
For residents, however, the immediate concern is the relentless heat.
From scorching afternoons to sticky nights, October has so far offered little relief—making it feel less like autumn and more like an extended summer.

articles.title: Odisha Universities Told to Fill Faculty Vacancies by November-End - businessnewsthisweek.com
articles.full_text:
Bhubaneswar, Oct. 4: Odisha Governor and Chancellor of state universities Dr Hari Babu Kambhampati has directed all state public universities to expedite the recruitment of teaching staff and complete the process by the end of November.
Pic Credit: //x.com/DHE_Odisha
The directive came during a high-level review meeting on faculty recruitment held at Lok Bhavan, where Vice-Chancellors and senior officials discussed the status of vacant teaching posts across universities.
The Governor asked universities to begin the recruitment process by the first week of November, leaving institutions with a clear deadline to complete appointments before the month ends.
Merit to Remain the Top Priority
Emphasising the importance of academic quality, Kambhampati said merit must remain the central consideration while selecting teaching faculty.
He stressed that universities should not compromise on the quality of appointments and must make every effort to attract the best available academic talent.
The Governor also suggested a recruitment approach aimed at ensuring wider participation by eligible candidates. Instead of eliminating large numbers of applicants at the initial scrutiny stage, universities could consider inviting all eligible candidates for interviews, allowing selection panels to assess their academic credentials and suitability more comprehensively.
Focus on Green and Sustainable Campuses
The meeting also covered issues beyond faculty recruitment, with the Governor encouraging universities to adopt sustainable practices on their campuses.
Referring to the IGBC Platinum Green certification received by Odisha Lok Bhavan, he urged universities to make better use of their existing green spaces and work towards obtaining similar green certifications.
